title: Development of the heart and great vessels

steps.tx: Septation divides the single atrium and ventricle. The **septum primum** grows downwards from the atrial roof and partly closes the **ostium primum**. Before it fuses, perforations form in its upper part and merge into the **ostium secundum**. The **septum secundum** then grows alongside it as a thicker, incomplete wall. The opening that persists is the **foramen ovale**, allowing right-to-left atrial shunting in fetal life. Most septal defects arise between weeks 6 and 8.
steps.say: Septation divides the single atrium and ventricle. The septum primum grows down from the roof of the atrium, and as its perforations merge they leave an opening called the ostium secundum. The septum secundum then grows alongside it. The gap that remains is the foramen ovale, which lets blood pass from the right atrium to the left atrium in fetal life. Septal defects develop mainly between six and eight weeks.

vis.alt: Flow diagram of atrial septation: septum primum grows down, the ostium primum closes, perforations form the ostium secundum, septum secundum grows beside it leaving the foramen ovale, which acts as a one-way flap.
vis.caption: Right-to-left flow through the foramen ovale bypasses the lungs in the fetus; the flap shuts at birth.

steps.tx: The **truncus arteriosus** and bulbus cordis are divided by the **aorticopulmonary septum**, which is formed by neural crest cells. This separates the aorta from the pulmonary trunk. The **endocardial cushions** divide the atrioventricular canal and contribute to the septa and valves, including the mitral and tricuspid leaflets. Failure of the tricuspid leaflets to attach to the annulus fibrosus causes Ebstein anomaly, while faulty aorticopulmonary septation causes persistent truncus arteriosus and tetralogy of Fallot.
steps.say: The truncus arteriosus and bulbus cordis are divided by the aorticopulmonary septum, which is formed by neural crest cells. This separates the aorta from the pulmonary trunk. The endocardial cushions divide the atrioventricular canal. Failure of the tricuspid leaflets to attach to the annulus fibrosus causes Ebstein anomaly. Faulty aorticopulmonary septation causes persistent truncus arteriosus and tetralogy of Fallot.

steps.tx: The six aortic arches do not exist together. The **first arch** gives the maxillary artery, the second gives the stapedial and hyoid arteries, and the **third arch** forms the common carotid arteries and the proximal internal carotid. The **fourth arch** gives the right subclavian artery proximal part on the right and the arch of aorta on the left. The **sixth arch** gives the pulmonary arteries, and the left distal part becomes the **ductus arteriosus**. The fifth arch is rudimentary and regresses.

steps.tx: In fetal life, oxygenated blood from the placenta returns through the **umbilical vein**, and most of it passes through the **ductus venosus** into the inferior vena cava. The **foramen ovale** shunts blood from right to left atrium, and the **ductus arteriosus** shunts blood from the pulmonary trunk to the aorta. The umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the iliac arteries back to the placenta. The cardiovascular system is the first system to function in the fetus.

steps.tx: After birth, lung aeration drops pulmonary resistance and clamping the cord raises systemic resistance. The **ductus arteriosus** constricts, mainly under falling prostaglandin levels, and is anatomically obliterated by intimal proliferation over 1 to 3 months. It then becomes the **ligamentum arteriosum**. A persistent ductus is a patent ductus arteriosus, which is acyanotic and treated with indomethacin or ibuprofen. The ductus venosus becomes the ligamentum venosum and the umbilical arteries become the medial umbilical ligaments.
steps.say: After birth, lung aeration lowers pulmonary resistance, and clamping the cord raises systemic resistance. The ductus arteriosus constricts as prostaglandin levels fall, and it is obliterated over one to three months. It then becomes the ligamentum arteriosum. A persistent ductus is a patent ductus arteriosus, treated with indomethacin or ibuprofen. The ductus venosus becomes the ligamentum venosum.

vis.alt: Table of fetal structures and their adult remnants: ductus arteriosus becomes ligamentum arteriosum, ductus venosus becomes ligamentum venosum, umbilical vein becomes ligamentum teres hepatis, umbilical arteries become medial umbilical ligaments, foramen ovale becomes fossa ovalis.
vis.caption: Every fetal shunt leaves a ligament or a fossa.
